name: Jeremiah Lee Mansion

dates.altered: Used as a bank 1804-1909; acquired and restored by the Marblehead Historical Society in 1909 (the survey's data form).

quotes.text: SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS OF STRUCTURE (SKETCHED FLOOR PLANS ON SEPARATE PAGES ARE ACCEPTABLE) Rectangular; 7-bay front; 3 stories; hipped roof; slightly projecting 3-bay pavilion on front; octagonal cupola EXTERIOR FEATURES OF NOTE V/ood quoins; 1st and 2nd floor windows have splayed wooden lintels with keystones; central pavilion is pedimented and lit by a lunnette; 1-story pedimented entrance porch supported by Ionic columns.
quotes.page: HABS No. MA-859, Architectural Data Form (Form 10-920, June 1983); no page number on the form

quotes.text: MATERIAL OF CONSTRUCTION (INCLUDE STRUCTURAL SYSTEMS) Frame, sheathed with rusticated boards to imitate stone
quotes.page: HABS No. MA-859, Architectural Data Form; no page number

quotes.text: SIGNIFICANCE (ARCHITECTURAL AND HISTORICAL, INCLUDE ORIGINAL USE OF STRUCTURE) One of the finest and most elaborate Georgian houses in the northern colonies. The grace and opulance of the house is physical documentation of the wealth and aspirations of New England merchant princes such as Jeremiah Lee.
quotes.page: HABS No. MA-859, Architectural Data Form; no page number

quotes.text: MAJOR ALTERATIONS AND ADDITIONS WITH DATES House was used as a bank from 1804-1909. Acquired and restored by the Marblehead Historical Society in 1909.
